chunks: Indeed God has helped you on many occasions, even during the battle of Hunain, when you were elated with joy at your numbers which did not prove of the least avail, so that the earth and its vast expanse became too narrow for you, and you turned back and retreated.

key_terms.حُنَيْنٍ: Hunain, a valley near Mecca where a significant battle took place.

ai.seo_question: What happened to the Muslim army at the Battle of Hunain despite their large numbers?
ai.summary: This verse, revealed in the context of the Battle of Hunain, serves as a divine corrective to the early Muslims' arrogance regarding their numerical strength, illustrating the transition from worldly confidence to spiritual humility. Shia exegetes, such as Al-Tabarsi, emphasize that the 'narrowing of the earth' signifies a moment of divine trial where physical vastness became a constraint, teaching believers that ultimate victory (Nasr) depends on God's will rather than material resources. It underscores the principle that even in moments of success, reliance on self (istikbar) can lead to temporary retreat until divine grace restores composure.
